items.text: The Public Relations of the Navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that from the early morning of Tuesday, 12 Aban, three 'violating' oil tankers suffered explosions and severe fires while passing through 'unauthorized routes' in the Strait of Hormuz. The tankers had turned off their navigation and identification systems and exploded due to hitting naval mines while passing through unauthorized routes in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US midterm elections have attracted the attention of German and Arab media. German media have examined inflation and the consequences of the Iran war as pressures on Republicans and the possibility of Democrats regaining Congress. Arab media have also addressed the potential implications of the elections for Donald Trump's political future, the Iran war, economic pressures, and Washington's foreign policy.

Ahmad Keyshams, a citizen from Izeh who was arrested in Aban 1404, was released from Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz on 27 Mehr 1405 with a bail arrangement. His release involved a 5 billion toman bail and a 500 million toman surety for another case.

Khodadad Azizi, the manager of Tractor football team, criticized the travel conditions of his team after the Asian Elite League match and asked the League Organization and Football Federation to postpone Tractor's match against Kheybar. He pointed to the heavy pressure on players and the likelihood of their injuries, saying the players need rest for the next game. Azizi also criticized the long travels of the team and said that under these conditions, there is no professional football in the Elite League for them.

According to ESPN, Jesus de Miguel, a 30-year-old striker for Spain's Tenerife team, suffered cardiac and respiratory arrest after a severe collision with the opposing goalkeeper during a second-division league match on Monday, November 2, and died on Tuesday. Following his death, the Spanish Football Federation postponed Tuesday's scheduled matches.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the refrigerator in his home and said: "There are a few eggs, some cheese, and a tomato paste left. The economic situation of the people of Iran is not good."

On the evening of Monday, 11 Aban, a number of women from the village of Tamp Rigan in Iranshahr County protested the drinking water cut and other livelihood problems by gathering in front of the village gas station, demanding attention to their demands.

Hossein Amoui, head of the Cemetery Management Organization of Qazvin Municipality, announced that the use of musical instruments and what is called "unconventional programs" is prohibited in cemeteries, surrounding areas, mosques, and other places of memorial ceremonies. This restriction is based on the resolutions of the Cemetery Supervision and Organization Working Group, and organizers and families of the deceased are also banned from using music in these ceremonies. This action effectively limits citizens' choices in how to hold mourning rituals.

Mohammad Rasoulof, an Iranian director, received the Akira Kurosawa Award at the end of the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival. He said at the ceremony that the people of Iran face daily executions and various forms of violence.

Prince Reza Pahlavi is meeting with several Belgian government officials and members of the European Parliament in Brussels and is scheduled to attend a press conference at the European Parliament. He will then travel to Germany to receive the Friedrich Naumann Foundation Freedom Award on behalf of the Iranian people. Concurrently with the start of this trip, a group of Prince Reza Pahlavi's supporters have gathered in Brussels.

Mohammad Javad Larijani said that "diplomacy and the field being side by side" is a joke and diplomacy must follow the path of resistance policy. He rejected Masoud Pezeshkian's statements about increasing government powers for negotiation and said Mojtaba Khamenei opposed nuclear negotiations. Larijani added that the current issue is "resistance or surrender," not war and peace, and that passing the law related to the Strait of Hormuz could have increased diplomats' bargaining power.

Majid Al-Ansari, spokesperson for Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said on Tuesday, 12 Aban, that his government hopes for a temporary agreement between the Islamic Republic and the United States. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran and the US still have a "long way" to go before reaching an agreement to end the war. Qatar is facilitating the exchange of proposals between the two sides, and mediators are working to reduce the gaps.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, warned neighbors on Tuesday, 12 Aban, that the Islamic Republic of Iran is ready for battle and has given a powerful response to the US. Ghalibaf also said Iran is at the highest level of defensive readiness and if Washington makes another strategic mistake, it will face a new battlefield. These statements came amid ongoing indirect talks between Tehran and Washington and a US Central Command bombing on Qeshm Island.

The newspaper Hamshahri, on 12 Aban 1405, published an illustration of US military bases in Europe, identifying them as potential missile targets of the Islamic Republic if a new war begins. The newspaper stated that the likelihood of the war expanding beyond the Middle East has increased and that US bases in Europe could be on Iran's list of potential targets.

On Tuesday, 12 Aban, Amjadieh Stadium hosted the final farewell to Hamid Alidousti, former national football team striker; the ceremony was held with the presence of prominent figures from Iranian football and art.

Mohammad Saleh Jokar, head of the Parliament's Councils Commission, said the newly tested missiles have longer range and can target moving objects. He added that if attacks come from US bases in Europe, those bases will also be targeted. Mohammad Seraj, a member of the Parliament's Social Commission, said the Islamic Republic has plans for a military response to US bases in Europe and that an unrestricted geographic military response authorization has been issued.

Leaders of four opposition parties to Benjamin Netanyahu agreed on Tuesday to immediately start negotiations to form a government coalition, but their path to a parliamentary majority remains unclear. These parties hold only 48 seats and need support from two Arab parties with 19 seats for a majority, but most have rejected the participation of Arab parties. Opposition leaders also agreed to support Gadi Eizenkot for the first mandate to form a government from Israeli President Isaac Herzog.

Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Berlin on an unannounced trip ahead of the meeting of representatives from Russia, the US, and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. Friedrich Merz and Zelensky are scheduled to discuss sending more military and financial aid to Kyiv.

Iran International asked its audience if, considering the experience of the 12-day and 40-day wars, they are preparing emergency backpacks this time as well. Most responses were negative, with many saying they neither have the financial means to prepare an emergency backpack nor a safe place to go. More details are provided in an interview with Seba Heydarkhani.
Two women's sports clubs in Zarand were sealed by the police due to what was described as "non-compliance with Islamic rules and modesty regulations regarding hijab and holding Halloween ceremonies."

Some citizens from Kohrang sent a video to Iran International requesting Iranians abroad to be present in Frankfurt on November 7 (Saturday, 16 Aban) simultaneously with the awarding of the German Freedom Prize to Prince Reza Pahlavi as a representative of the Iranian nation, to create a heroic event.

The prosecutor of Qaenat reported the closure of a cafe-restaurant and a sports club in this county. The announced reasons for the closure of these units included holding Halloween ceremonies and the promotional use of an image of a woman without mandatory hijab.

Voting has begun in electoral districts across the United States. In this election, voters decide the fate of 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 out of 100 seats in the Senate. Maryam Rahmati, an Iran International reporter, reports from Columbus, Ohio.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported receiving a report from the Indian government about an attack on an Indian sailing vessel on 11 Aban 1405. The Omani Navy rescued the surviving crew, but the ship's condition remains unknown. The UK center advised vessels to pass the area cautiously and report suspicious activities.

Trump said that last night they targeted an air defense facility that had taken two months to build. He emphasized that this attack was not a major war and added that a real war has not yet occurred. Trump also spoke about Iran's situation and its nuclear program.

Prince Reza Pahlavi met with Christophe Gomar, Vice-Chair of the Security and Defense Committee of the European Parliament, in Brussels on Tuesday, 12 Aban. They discussed ways to support the people of Iran. Gomar expressed strong support for the Iranian people and their struggle against the Islamic Republic, and both sides explored practical ways to support Iranians, including helping maintain access to free internet.

Majid Saeedi, a photojournalist, has been detained by security forces in Tehran for 56 days, and his place of detention remains unknown. According to the HRANA news agency, the lack of information about his fate continues. There is also no information about the detaining authority or the status of his case.

Donald Trump said the US targeted an Iranian air defense system last night that took about two months to build and was under US surveillance. He added that Iran was close to obtaining nuclear weapons and the US will cut $4 billion aid to Israel at the end of the year. Trump also said he is not seeking war but will act if forced.

A video received by Iran International on Tuesday, 12 Aban, shows the moment Prince Reza Pahlavi's arrival at the European Parliament in Brussels. He met with some members of the European Parliament during this trip. It was also announced that Prince Reza Pahlavi will speak about the Middle East at the Royal Military Academy of Belgium on Friday, 15 Aban.

Ibrahim Haydan, Yemen's Interior Minister, said 21 experts affiliated with the IRGC and Hezbollah Lebanon operate in areas controlled by the Houthis and play roles in directing military operations, developing armament capabilities, and planning naval attacks of the group. He stated that 14 of these individuals are members of the IRGC and seven are Hezbollah forces. These experts operate in various Yemeni provinces and specialize in managing military operations, ballistic missiles, drones, and electronic warfare.

Eight flights in various European countries, including three from the UK, were targeted by possible bomb threats within the past 24 hours, and some were forced to make emergency landings. Two Ryanair planes from Lisbon and Dublin were inspected after landing in Rome, with the Dublin flight escorted by the Italian Air Force. Additionally, flights from London, Manchester, Italy, and Ireland were inspected after receiving threats, and a flight from Luton London to Sofia made an emergency landing in Budapest due to a bomb threat.

Zartosht Ahmadi Ragheb and Masoud Farhikhteh, political prisoners in Karaj Central Prison, have been deprived of phone contact for about a month. Their families have pursued inquiries but have not received any response so far. This situation has increased the families' concerns about the detention conditions and health of the prisoners.

Reza Rostaei, Director General of Performance Evaluation at the Ministry of Education, announced the cancellation of the managerial order of the principal of Andimeshk Boys' Shahed School due to physical punishment of students. After a video showing the principal's physical confrontation with students was released, an inspection team acted and confirmed the principal's misconduct, leading to the cancellation of his managerial order. The principal's case has been referred to the Administrative Violations Board for further review.

Kazem Gharibabadi, Deputy Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, said on Tuesday, 12 Aban, that the United States has not yet taken an official position on the use of nuclear weapons, but it knows the consequences of threatening to use such weapons.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, announced on Tuesday, 12 Aban, that the US response to Iran's rights and demands was not convincing. He said the US must fully and explicitly respond to Iran's seven conditions and comply with them for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen. Although Qatari mediators have presented a new peace plan, it appears Tehran has not agreed to it.

The director general of forensic medicine in Markazi province reported the death of 367 people and injury of 4,195 people in traffic accidents in the province during the first six months of the current year. Among the injured, 2,887 were men and 1,308 were women. The monthly number of victims increased from 55 in Farvardin to 74 in Shahrivar.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic, said on Tuesday, 12 Aban, that Iran participates in any diplomatic process with maximum caution and complete skepticism. He added that the US attacked Iran twice during negotiations in less than a year and violated its commitments just weeks after the Islamabad agreement. Baqaei also said Iran has no fear of diplomacy and sees negotiation as a tool to secure national interests and prevent the escalation of insecurity in the region.

Prince Reza Pahlavi, during his European trip in Brussels, warned about the wave of executions in Iran and said it is now time to help the Iranian people end this regime of terror. At the same time, a group of Iranians supporting Prince Reza Pahlavi held a gathering to express their support.

Donald Trump said that US forces completely destroyed the Islamic Republic's air defense in a limited attack on the night of Monday, 11 Aban. He added that the construction of this system took two months, and after completion, US forces destroyed it. Trump also said the Islamic Republic no longer has aircraft or air defense systems.

Etemad newspaper reported on the shortage of nursing staff, insufficient wages, delays in payment of claims, and job burnout among nurses. According to statistics announced by the Deputy Nursing Minister of Health, last year 1800 nurses left their jobs, 800 resigned, 1600 retired, and 380 emigrated. The shortage of staff has led to longer shifts and mandatory overtime, which is linked to increased medical errors and threats to patient safety.

Qalibaf warned that Tehran's response to a possible US attack would be unpredictable. The Russian foreign minister said there are deeply worrying signs of planning for an attack on Iran. Trump and Pence appear optimistic about negotiations.

A citizen posted a video showing that officials at the 'Shahedan Tajalli' elementary school in Shiraz demand money from the family to provide their son's report card. School officials say the Ministry of Education only stated that school registration is free.

Mohsen Ghadimi, the brother of Mehdi Ghadimi, a 26-year-old footballer who was killed by the Islamic Republic's suppression forces on 19 Dey 1404 in Fereydunkenar, published an image of his playing card issued for the Mazandaran province football club championship. This card is from the 1401/2 season of the adult first division football league of the province. He had previously released a video of Mehdi's phone conversation with his father on the morning of 19 Dey.

An official in Iran's foreign trade sector pointed to widespread disruptions at the Pakistan and Turkey borders and said that land corridors for foreign trade are defined only on paper, and this situation has caused the cost of goods transportation to multiply. This is an assessment by Masoumeh Taherkhani, an economic analyst.

According to a version of the directive received by Iran International, the Islamic Republic's Ministry of Education has brought global political tensions into schools. The government encourages students to align with its policies regarding the necessity of American forces leaving the region. It also forces students to participate in government nighttime gatherings.
The number of detainees in Piranshahr increased to two with the arrest of Sadegh Abubakri, a citizen of Piranshahr, on Monday, 11 Aban.

Hadi Jalali, a teacher and political prisoner in Jiroft prison, ended his hunger strike. This action followed officials' promise to address his demands, including medical care and access to his medications. This occurred on Monday, 11 Aban.
A video received by Iran International shows that the military base "Reza Hasanpour Operational Headquarters" in Qazvin is located next to schools.

Halvash reported that from 10 Aban 1405 [Gregorian: 2026-11-01], dozens of students at the University of Sistan and Baluchestan have been summoned to the Intelligence Department, and some have been suspended for two semesters. Accusations such as "leadership," "creating unrest at the university," and "mercenary work" have been made against the students, and some have been pressured to give forced confessions. The university disciplinary committee has provided student information to the Intelligence Department, and concerns about new suspension and expulsion orders have increased.

Roya Eidi-Nejad, sister of Zahra Eidi-Nejad who died in the January protests, was arrested on 3 Mehr by IRGC intelligence agents in Quchan and remains in uncertainty. Judicial officials have not provided clear information about her case status, and her temporary detention has recently been extended.
The results of the US midterm congressional elections could affect Donald Trump's foreign policy and Washington's relations with Israel. More details with Babak Es-haqi, Iran International reporter.

Reuters reported that a bomb threat on the cruise ship "Crown Iris" at the port of Syros Island, Greece, on Tuesday, 12 Aban, led to security operations. Initial inspections found no explosive devices. Also, at least seven flights in Europe faced bomb threats on Tuesday, causing airport disruptions but no explosives were found.

Arash Aramesh, a legal expert and national security analyst, said that if the Democrats win and gain the majority in the U.S. House of Representatives, Donald Trump will face more political restrictions and pressures, but this does not necessarily mean a fundamental change in his administration's foreign policy.

The competition between Republicans and Democrats to control the House of Representatives and the Senate in the US midterm elections is ongoing. At the same time, the race for governors in Alaska, Nevada, Georgia, and Wisconsin is considered close.

39 dismissed workers of the contracting company Jahan Pars in Ilam have not returned to work despite a ruling to return. About 200 workers of the Central Rabat iron ore mine in Ardakan remain uncertain after the temporary closure of the mine. Bampur sanitation workers complain about unpaid wages for four months and insurance rights for one year and five months, and cooperation of Pezhvak Energy company with more than 30 of its employees has been cut off.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the deputy speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, said that any place under the control of the United States that helps it in military, economic, or technological fields is considered a target for attack by the Islamic Republic. He added that the war with the US and Israel has extended beyond the military to economic, perceptual, and cognitive domains. He also emphasized that anyone cooperating with the US is considered an opponent of the Islamic Republic, and if Iran's oil is sanctioned, then all oil should be sanctioned.

Fereshteh Pezeshk, an international relations expert, said the Democrats' effort to unite a broad spectrum of supporters under one political umbrella in the US midterm elections could become problematic due to deep divisions in American society. She said if Democrats and Republicans cannot manage differences among their supporters, both parties will face serious challenges.

The death sentence of a man convicted of complicity in murder in Tehran was confirmed by the Supreme Court. Also, a defendant in the case of killing his wife in Fariman was sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Criminal Court One of Khorasan Razavi.

Mehdi Taj, the head of the Football Federation, announced that Amir Ghalenoei will continue as the national team coach until the 2027 Asian Cup. The Asian Cup has been postponed by one year due to ongoing attacks by Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic. Taj also promised that Ghalenoei will implement serious youth development in the national team and confirmed that the Iranian Hazfi Cup will be held with the postponement of the Asian Cup.

At least two protest gatherings were held today, Tuesday, 12 Aban, including a group of Tehran sanitation workers protesting in front of the city municipality over unfulfilled promises of status changes. Also, a group of workers at the Benro company in Saveh went on strike over unpaid months of wages and demands. Students of the Faculty of Social Sciences at the University of Tehran staged a sit-in demanding the release of detained students and political prisoners and the halt of disciplinary sentences.

On the eve of the US midterm elections, Republicans hold the majority in both chambers of Congress. A change in the House of Representatives' composition and Democrats gaining the majority could lead to investigations into the Trump administration's performance and make passing bills and the federal budget more difficult. If the government and Congress do not agree on the budget, a government shutdown is also possible.

Ahmad Hayat Moghadam, Vice-Chairman of the National Security Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, announced that four countries—India, China, Iraq, and Qatar—have been exempted from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz, and their ships freely pass through this waterway. The Islamic Republic does not collect transit fees from Qatar. The exemption for India is intended to allow medicine imports, and the decision regarding China aims to gain political support.
A student from Kermanshah sent a video to Iran International showing forms for "parental consent" and said students were forced to participate in the official ceremony on 13 Aban [2026-11-04].

The New York Times reported, citing American and regional officials, that Israel has provided the US with intelligence about the possibility of the Islamic Republic using chemical weapons. This information has met concern and serious doubt among some American officials. Israel has also shared part of this intelligence with Gulf countries.

Kambiz Tavana, a reporter for Iran International, reported from Virginia that the close competition among House of Representatives candidates in this state could play a role in maintaining or losing the Republican majority. According to him, the presence of senior figures from both parties in the Virginia Beach election campaigns, including Mike Johnson, Speaker of the House, Hakeem Jeffries, and Chuck Schumer, indicates the importance of this competition.

The Spanish Football Federation suspended all matches under its supervision until November 6 following the death of Jesús de Miguel, the 30-year-old Tenerife forward. This decision was made to pay tribute to the deceased player and express condolences to his family and Tenerife club. The men's and women's Spanish Cup matches scheduled for this week were postponed.

Reza Gheysipour, the Director General of Khuzestan Standards, warned against the use of worn-out, non-standard playground equipment lacking safety approval in parks, amusement parks, schools, kindergartens, and recreational centers. He called for the cessation of the use of these devices. He said that failure to comply with safety standards in the design, construction, installation, and operation of these devices could endanger children's health and lead to accidents and physical injuries.
Iran International reported that the topic of financial supporters of the US midterm elections has been raised.

Ali Akbar Alvandian, secretary of the Cement Industry Employers Association, announced that gas supply to all cement factories has been completely cut off since the first of Aban, and these factories are using mazut for fuel. He added that since the beginning of the year, cement factories faced an 80% gas supply limitation, receiving only 5 to 6 million cubic meters of gas daily out of the 28 million cubic meters needed. According to the secretary of the Cement Industry Employers Association, since the first of Aban, even this amount of gas has been cut off, and the gas quota for cement factories has reached zero.

Mousa al-Reza Zoghi Moghadam, a 64-year-old resident of Mashhad, was released from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on 6 Aban with a bail order. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency. His release took place on the evening of the same day.

Ali Sadrazadeh, a Middle East analyst, said Gulf countries are concerned that if a conflict occurs between the US and the Islamic Republic, they will be targeted by the Islamic Republic and suffer the most damage. He added that these concerns have overshadowed the regional countries' views on the policies of the Republican and Democratic parties towards Iran and the region ahead of the US midterm elections.

Negar Mojtahedi, a reporter for Iran International, received the 2026 Bill Good Award at the 40th annual Webster Awards in Vancouver for her reporting on war, government violence, and human rights violations in Iran. She received the award at the November 2 ceremony and dedicated it to the people of Iran, especially those who lost their lives seeking freedom. Mojtahedi emphasized the serious dangers journalists face under the Islamic Republic's rule.

The Democratic Socialists of America have expanded in recent years and support candidates close to their views in elections. In this year's House of Representatives elections, 10 candidates are either members of or supported by this organization.
Shayan Samiei, a national security expert, said the end of the midterm elections will give Trump more freedom to make decisions about the Islamic Republic and move towards military confrontation.

The US midterm elections, besides determining control of Congress, are a test of the impact of Donald Trump's electoral support; he has supported about 300 candidates, including 218 House of Representatives candidates and 30 Senate candidates.

Sky News Arabia reported that several municipalities in northern Israel have decided to open shelters and that parking lots of major hospitals have been evacuated to be converted into emergency departments. These measures are reported as preparations for a possible war with the Islamic Republic and Hezbollah.

The head coach of Esteghlal said after the victory against Al Shamal that even the greatest players in the world may make mistakes in the final shot, but this issue is solvable. He expressed satisfaction with his team's result and performance in the second half, stating they played excellent football. He also mentioned that the spectators enjoyed Esteghlal's brave play in the second half.

Reports indicate that in Kermanshah schools, forms have been distributed for mandatory student participation in rallies. In Malayer, the Saif al-Dawla girls' school has suspended teaching and turned into a Basij base. In Karaj and Abrisham town, students are being forced to attend rallies on 13 Aban under threat of grade deductions.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center has received a report of an incident 14 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman. A security officer of the company owning an oil tanker reported that two unidentified projectiles hit the engine room of the tanker.

Tonight, before the UEFA Champions League matches, players and attendees in the stadiums observed a minute of silence in memory of Jesus de Miguel, a Tenerife player. This player suffered a cardiac arrest and died yesterday after a collision during the match between Tenerife and Andorra in the Spanish second division league.

APA news agency of Azerbaijan announced that the country has declared 14 Iranians, including members of the Islamic Republic's parliament, clerics, and media figures, as "undesirable elements" and banned their entry into the country. This decision was made following statements and positions that Azerbaijani officials assessed as against the sovereignty, security, and constitutional order of the country. Those subject to this restriction are accused of making statements against the government and leaders of Azerbaijan, criticizing the governance structure and government-religion relations, promoting religious extremism, and demanding the forced removal of officials in the country.

Kambiz Tavana, an Iran International reporter, conducted a special interview with Vida Mehrannia, wife of Ahmadreza Jalali, about his latest condition in prison and actions the international community and human rights organizations can take to save his life. Ahmadreza Jalali was arrested in Ordibehesht 1395 after traveling to Iran at the invitation of Tehran and Shiraz universities and was accused of espionage. Vida Mehrannia said in the interview that her husband's physical and mental condition is severely poor because he has spent many years in prison, much of it in solitary confinement, and his repeated requests for retrial have been ignored.

Prince Reza Pahlavi left the European Parliament building after about 9 hours of presence in Brussels and meetings with several members of the parliament. He discussed ways to support the people of Iran with Christophe Goumard, Vice-President of the European Parliament's Security and Defense Committee. At the same time, a group of Iranians gathered outside the parliament to express their support for Prince Reza Pahlavi.
A citizen released a video of Iranians gathering in front of the British Prime Minister's office in London on Tuesday, protesting executions and against the Islamic Republic.

The race for a U.S. Senate seat in Michigan has drawn attention to Abdol El-Sayed, a Muslim Democratic candidate, who reportedly declined to condemn the Revolutionary Guards in response to a direct question from an Iranian-American student at a Q&A session at the University of Michigan.

Amir Hayatmoghadam, vice-chairman of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the parliament, said the Islamic Republic is seeking to increase the range of its missiles and has asked the defense minister to take action to produce intercontinental missiles. He added that the Ministry of Defense and the IRGC are ready to produce missiles with a range of six thousand kilometers in the first phase and then increase the missile range to reach the United States.

The war with the Islamic Republic and its economic consequences, including rising fuel prices and living costs, have become a key issue in the US midterm elections. It has been discussed how much Democrats could limit Donald Trump's policies towards Tehran if they gain control of one or both houses of Congress. An interview with Omid Memarian and Behnam Taleblou has been conducted on this topic.

The Iran Human Rights Organization reported that at least 77 people were executed in Iran in October. Six were executed on security charges and three detainees from the nationwide protests in Dey month were executed during this period. Additionally, at least 691 executions have been recorded in the past 10 months, including three males under 18 at the time of their alleged crimes, 23 women, and 28 foreign nationals.

In one of the voting districts in Virginia Beach, a designated area around the polling place has been set to prevent election campaigning. No party advertisements are allowed in this area, and Republican and Democratic representatives must also speak with voters outside of it.

Sebastian Tynkkynen, Finland's representative in the European Parliament, posted a photo of his meeting with Prince Reza Pahlavi, writing that the prince's struggle for his people truly inspires him and that he wants to end the Islamic Republic's rule once and for all. Tynkkynen said no to the EU's official policy of appeasement with the mullahs and supported recognizing the voice of the Iranian people for regime change.

Anil Menon, a NASA astronaut, voted in the US midterm elections from the International Space Station. He said he filled out his electronic ballot with a computer and sent it to election officials in Harris County, Texas. According to Menon, all three American astronauts present on the station were able to vote.

In the US midterm elections, all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 Senate seats are up for vote. The outcome of this election will determine control of both chambers and the legislative and oversight path over the Trump administration in the remaining two years of his presidency.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said he considers the likelihood of resuming war between the US and the Islamic Republic higher than reaching an agreement. He added that the outcome of the midterm elections and the future composition of Congress could make Trump's military decisions easier or harder.

Donald Trump told Financial Times that the United States has no immediate plans to attack Iran and considers the current situation with Tehran satisfactory. He added that the US is ready but there may be no reason for an attack and emphasized that indirect talks about Iran's enriched uranium reserves continue. Trump also said more oil is passing through the Strait of Hormuz and the blockade of Iranian ports is weakening Tehran's economy.
Voting ended in Ohio; a close race between two parties for the former JD Vance Senate seat was reported. This report was provided by Maryam Rahmati from Iran International.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the Islamic Republic uses asymmetric warfare tactics, including underwater drones carrying explosives, sticky mines, and small boats, to disrupt ship traffic and oil transport from the Persian Gulf. The newspaper cited regional officials and military experts saying Tehran seeks to regain control of the Strait of Hormuz and increase pressure on the Donald Trump administration through these methods. In recent weeks, Islamic Republic forces have fired rocket grenades and attached explosives to commercial ships in addition to using underwater drones.

Michigan, an industrial state in the US and a key state in the 2016 and 2024 presidential elections, is tonight the scene of a Senate seat race. Abdul, the Democratic candidate, if victorious, will become the first Muslim senator in US history.

Roy Cooper, the Democratic Party candidate, won the North Carolina Senate seat in the US midterm elections and delivered a victory speech to his supporters at the Marriott Hotel in Raleigh. With Cooper's victory, Democrats won the state's Senate election for the first time since 2008. This victory is important for the Democrats' efforts to gain a majority in the Senate, although the final results of the congressional races in several states are still unknown.

Shahram Khaledi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, said that Israel's shift away from past social-democratic tendencies toward the right, alongside the U.S. Democratic Party's shift to the left, has influenced American voters' views of Israel.

Omid Memarian, journalist and political analyst, referring to the Republican defeat in the US midterm elections, said Donald Trump might resort to a severe and striking military action against the Islamic Republic to end the war faster. According to Memarian, Trump might seek to record a military achievement and declare victory before the new Congress begins and Democratic oversight increases.

Donald Trump did not accept responsibility for the performance of Republican candidates as Democrats increased their seats in the midterm elections. He wrote on Truth Social that his name was not on the ballot, and if it had been, they would have won by a large margin. Associated Press reported that Trump, who followed the results with political advisors and cabinet members at the White House, had campaigned for many Republican candidates before the elections and asked voters to imagine his name was on the ballot.

Josh Shulman, a Democratic member of the Virginia Beach City Council, emphasized in an interview with Kambiz Tavana that dissatisfaction with the president's performance, even among some Republicans, has increased people's motivation to participate widely in the elections.

CNN and CBS networks announced that based on their assessment, the Democrats have gained the majority of seats in the US House of Representatives. NBC network also predicted that this party will control the House with 241 seats against 191 seats for the Republicans.
James Talarico, the Democratic candidate, ended Republican dominance in Texas by winning the Senate election. This is the first victory for a Democrat in a statewide Texas election since 1994.

Donald Trump acknowledged that the war with Iran played a role in the Republicans' defeat in the Tuesday midterm elections. He told Fox News that Democrats will send "crazy" bills to the White House for signature and he will veto them. Trump also said people probably could not accept the short-term gasoline price consequences after the Iran war and announced he does not intend to change his cabinet composition.

With the continued counting of votes in the US midterm elections, Democrats succeeded in gaining the Senate majority and reclaiming control of this chamber from Republicans after two years. Preliminary results also indicate Democrats leading in the House of Representatives; estimates show the party is on the verge of controlling both chambers of Congress.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, described the Democrats' success in the US midterm elections as the American people's "no" to war. Ghalibaf said Americans said no to war either because of conscience or living costs, and we support this message. He warned that if the US government betrays its people's will, Iran's "no" will bring a nightmare.

Alireza Salimi, a member of the Parliament's presidium, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, that the Islamic Republic today has more power and can strike all US interests in any geographical area it chooses. He added that from the Islamic Republic's perspective, there is no difference between the two US political parties in terms of bullying. Salimi also said that the US election results showed how influential the Islamic Republic is in global equations and even in the internal developments of the US.

Amir Hamidi, a national security expert, said the results of the US midterm elections indicate dissatisfaction among part of the American society with the economic situation and the performance of the Trump administration. He emphasized that the Republican electoral defeat does not mean the end of Trump's power or a strategic weakening of the US. He also warned that a miscalculation by the Islamic Republic in assessing Washington's power could have a heavy cost for Tehran.

Reza Arab, a political analyst, said that the meetings of Prince Reza Pahlavi with members of the European Parliament show that the voice of the Iranian people has been heard in European political circles. He emphasized the need to end Europe's appeasement policy towards the Islamic Republic and said that the plan to overthrow the Islamic Republic, manage the transition period, establish secular democracy, and preserve Iran's territorial integrity were the main focuses of these meetings.

According to American media, Gina Hinojosa, a Democratic member of the Texas State House of Representatives, defeated Greg Abbott, the Republican governor of the state, in the gubernatorial election, ending three decades of Republican control over the position. Hinojosa will be the first Latinx governor of Texas. Democrats are on track to gain control of the House and Senate in this election and have also won in conservative states like South Carolina and Kansas.

The US midterm elections have raised concerns about the future of Washington's relations with Asia-Pacific countries. The war with the Islamic Republic, the energy crisis, and Trump's administration's trade tariffs are main factors behind these concerns. This report is by Alireza Mohibi from Iran International.
The prosecutor of Astara reported the arrest of a citizen in this county due to sending surveillance camera images of the city to foreign media.
A video released by state media shows a group of regime supporters in Tehran threatening to kill the U.S. president with slogans "Khamenei is the leader" and "We will kill Trump."

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, said that the United States and Israel have been defeated and cooperating with US plans means artificial respiration to a defeated enemy and preparing the ground for the next attack on Iran. He added that Europe and countries that supported the US in the region owe the Iranian nation and should apologize and compensate for the damages to the Iranian people.

The Kerman Revolutionary Court sentenced three Baha'i citizens, Venus Hosseini-Nejad, Shakila Ghasemi, and Adib Shahbazpour, to a total of 24 years in prison. Each of them was sentenced to eight years in prison. This ruling was issued by the Fifth Branch of the Kerman Revolutionary Court.

A citizen reported to Iran International via a video that they bought two packs of treatment capsules for more than 3.5 million tomans and that it was difficult to afford and pay this amount with a retirement pension.

Joachim Wadephul, Germany's Foreign Minister, identified the Islamic Republic as the main cause of current conflicts and said Tehran's actions have paved the way for military responses from other countries. He stated that the Islamic Republic is preparing to acquire nuclear weapons and supports paramilitary groups in neighboring countries. The German Foreign Minister emphasized that the Islamic Republic's behavior is neither harmless nor friendly and may provoke a military reaction.

The prosecutor of Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province announced the issuance of an indictment against the principal of the private 'Saoud' school in Shahr-e Kord and other individuals related to the case of a dance video published online. The video shows dancing inside the school, which domestic media described as "behavior unbecoming of an educational environment."
30 students in Miandoab were hospitalized due to symptoms of poisoning. The cause of the poisoning has not yet been determined and the matter is under investigation.

Johan Wadephul, Germany's Foreign Minister, said that due to good relations, Germany's voice is heard in Israel and the US. He added that he does not insist on talks with Iran's Foreign Minister and that regime change in Iran is only possible from within the country. Wadephul also recalled Germany's special responsibility towards Israel.

The head of the Iranian Psychiatric Association stated that rising treatment costs and shortages of psychiatric drugs have led some patients to reduce their medication intake and visit doctors less frequently. Seyed Vahid Shariat said that some psychiatric drugs in the country have become scarce. He warned that reducing or stopping medication could lead to disease relapse and increased hospitalization needs in the coming months.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said the results of the US midterm elections could increase Trump's motivation to end the Islamic Republic case. He added Trump might resort to an imposed agreement on Tehran or a widespread war to achieve this goal.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, called the statements of the Speaker of the Islamic Republic's parliament about the US elections ironic and shameful. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic has not even allowed a referendum on important national issues. Kazemian also considered the government media's enthusiasm over the Republicans' defeat as stemming from the illusion that the Democrats' victory could change US policy towards the Islamic Republic.
A retiree sent a video to Iran International reporting the price of potatoes and comparing inflation in Iran and the US, saying: "Let's judge which economy has collapsed and who has failed."

Shin Bet announced that preliminary information indicates possible foreign funding and extensive interference in Israel's elections involving "thousands and possibly more". The agency said the financial sources for these activities came from foreign countries and actors with "hidden and even hostile interests." Itamar Ben-Gvir called for the arrest of Arab party leaders and the immediate halt of final election result certification.

Ziaeddin Aghajanpour, head of the Ideological-Political Organization of the Ministry of Defense, said at the November 4 ceremony in Karaj that the Ministry of Defense and the armed forces have produced astonishing weapons, and their missiles can target areas beyond the Middle East. He also warned that if the Americans do not stop their mischief, all American interests in the region will be targeted. Aghajanpour referred to the killing of Ali Khamenei at the beginning of the 40-day war and said he was among the special saints of God.

Hamidreza Moghaddamfar, advisor to the commander of the IRGC, said at the November 4 ceremony in Bandar Abbas that if countries like the UAE and Bahrain provide bases for attacks on Iran to the US, the IRGC's attacks will be beyond just targeting bases and will be more instructive. He added that the IRGC's responses will no longer be proportional and will target the assets of their enemies. He also warned that if Iranian commanders and leaders are targeted, the enemies should expect their own commanders and leaders to be killed.

The Democratic Party took back the majority in the Senate and House of Representatives from Republicans in the US midterm elections. Based on announced results, Democrats have so far taken 54 Senate seats, while Republicans have obtained 42 seats.

Roland Lescure, the French Minister of Economy and Finance, said on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, in response to the Republican defeat in the US midterm elections, that President Donald Trump still has the authority to make decisions on foreign policy and his behavior is unpredictable. Lescure told French TV channel BFM that Trump either decides to rise above political conflicts and reduce his intervention in international affairs, or he does not. He added that this is an issue that needs to be closely monitored in the coming days.

According to reports, Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic candidate, won the Michigan State Senate seat in the US midterm elections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Media outlets predicted that El-Sayed, 42, defeated Mike Rogers, a Republican candidate backed by Donald Trump, and retained the seat of retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters for his party. El-Sayed had previously called Israel's war in Gaza "genocide" and opposed war against the Islamic Republic.

Some Iran International viewers criticized the Islamic Republic officials' stance on the US midterm election results in response to the Democrats' victory. They pointed out that with two years remaining in Donald Trump's presidency, the change in congressional majority does not necessarily mean a change in US policies towards the Islamic Republic.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said Trump is under pressure to end the war with the Islamic Republic quickly to avoid repeating the Republican defeat in the next election. He rejected the possibility of a minimal agreement between Tehran and Washington and added that Trump must either achieve regime change in Iran or eliminate the threat capability of the Islamic Republic and the Revolutionary Guards.

Parliament members approved articles in a bill titled "Combating the infiltration of intelligence services and foreign governments or institutions" allowing courts to punish or dissolve a legal entity if a crime is committed using its name or facilities. Also, if a person commits a criminal act due to negligence harming national security or interests, they face a fifth or sixth degree punishment. If two or more conspire to commit crimes under this bill, each person's punishment can increase by one to two degrees.
